caseno: Criminal Miscellaneous Case 7460, 7403, 7461 of 2002 with Criminal Miscellaneous Case 248 of 2003
lawyer:
AKM Nazrul Islam, Advocate, with Md Ozair Farooque, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Md Helal Uddin Mollah, Deputy Attorney-General with Md Ibrahim Khalil, Assistant Attorney-General—For the State-Respondent
full_judgment:
2. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7460 of 2002, the petitioner challenged the proceeding of Khulshi PS Case No. 40(6) 2002 dated 30-6-2002 corresponding to DAB, GR Case No. 12 of 2002, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7461 of 2002 the petitioner challenged the proceeding of Khulshi PS Case No. 41(6) 2002 dated 30-6-2002 corresponding to DAB, GR Case No. 13 of 2002, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7403 of 2002 the petitioner challenged the proceeding of Khulshi PS Case No. 42(6) 2002 dated 30-6-2002 corresponding to DAB, GR Case No. 14 of 2002 and in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 248 of 2003 the petitioner challenged the proceeding of Khulshi PS Case No. 32(9) 2002 dated 25-9-2002 corresponding to DAB, GR Case No. 27 of 2002 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong and prayed for quashment of the said proceedings so far as it relates to the petitioner. 

 3. In all these cases it has been alleged that accused petitioner gave allotment of a Government property without following the provision of rules and regulations thereby getting pecuniary advantage punishable under sections 409/420/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. In all those Rules the petitioner placed unnecessary voluminous supplementary affidavit placing some materials, which, according to us, are not relevant for the disposal of these Rules and we left out of our consideration the said supplementary affidavits. 

 4. The facts of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7460 of 2002 are that the petitioner at the relevant time was the Deputy Commissioner of Chittagong (now on retirement) along with 3 others, of them accused No. 2 and accused No. 3 are Government Officers, for their own benefit, in between 11-4-2000 and 24-9-2000 by malpractice, allotted plot No. 8 of Lane No. 5, road No. 1, Block L compromising an area of 400 square yards without any sanction of the relevant Ministry, to accused No. 4. It has been alleged in the lengthy first information report filed by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption that the said plot was earlier allotted to one Nur Miah Master, later on Nur Miah Master having defaulted his allotment was cancelled on 25-7-2001. Thereafter, Asaduzzaman, a relation of accused No. 2, Administrative Officer, applied for the said plot on 11-4-2002 to the allotment committee of which the accused petitioner was the Chairman, who on 16-4-2000 provisionally accepted the said allotment on condition if the committee gave approval of the same. As per said instruction, the Administrative Officer, accused No. 2 and accused No. 3, an Assistant of the Housing Estate, prepared note to which the accused petitioner on 23-4-2000 gave approval. It has further been alleged that the said approval was given by the accused petitioner without getting any clearance from the relevant Ministry. As per Memo No. Sha-9/6L-6/98/222 /1(80) dated 9-8-2000, it was circulated that allotment of plots can be given only on approval of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works and Urban Development. Despite knowing about the aforesaid circular, the accused petitioner held a meeting on 10-8-2002 but in that meeting, no discussion was made on this plot, but later on, it transpired that in this meeting, this plot was allotted to accused No. 4. It has been further alleged in the first information report that from the foregoing facts, it appears in the said meeting plots were not allotted to anybody but later on, by malpractice, the plots were allotted. 

 5. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7461 of 2002 the facts are similar but it relates to plot No. 2/B, Lane 5, Road No. 2, Block K and this plot was allotted to one Mokhlesur Rahman, accused No. 4, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7403 of 2002 the facts are similar but it relates to plot No. 10, Lane No. 3, Road No. 2, Block K and it was allotted to accused No. 4, HM Ibrahim, and in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 248 of 2003 the plot is A-6, Block G. Halishahar Housing Estate, Chittagong and this plot was allotted to a school which is now running. 

 6. The accused petitioner in all these cases appeared before the learned Magistrate and after he was enlarged on bail, moved this court. 

 7. In all these cases police has not yet submitted report. A question may be raised that before submitting of police report whether a case can be quashed. As per decision of 28 DLR (AD) 38 if it is seen from the narration of facts of the first information report, if no case is made out against the accused or the facts are preposterous, in that case, the accused can invoke the provision of section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure without waiting for police report. 

 8. In the instant case we find first information report was lodged by Bureau of Anti-Corruption on 30-6-2002 but the State till today, cannot satisfy us as to whether the police report has been submitted or not. It is an harassment of an innocent. In this case State verbally made submission but in such type of case, verbal submission is not enough as State must deny the facts in writing because it appears that accused is now a retired government servant and he has been dragging in a case made by the informant, i.e. Bureau of Anti-Corruption, after his retirement. Since Government did not controvert the statements made in the Rule petition, we may take them as true. 

 Section 5—Criminal Misconduct 

 (1) A public servant is said to commit the offence of criminal misconduct— 

 13. From the aforesaid provision, it appears that if any public servant in any way abusing his position as public servant obtains or attempts to obtain for himself or for any other person any valuable thing or pecuniary advantage is said to commit the offence of misconduct punishable under the law. 

 14. It therefore, appears to us that there was no criminal intention on the part of the accused-petitioner at any stage of deliberations in taking the decision for the allotment of the disputed plots. Criminal intention is sine qua non for an offence under section 5(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. When a decision is taken collectively or even individually by following the rules of procedure or the rules of business, criminal intention behind such decision should not normally be inferred. If any loss is incurred or suffered on account of such decision that can at best give rise to a civil liability and not criminal liability. Because such a loss can be considered to have been caused due to misjudgment or lack of due care on the part of the person or persons who took the decision. We do not find the accused petitioner had any criminal intent in taking the decision to allot the plots. Rather, we find that the informant of this case has deliberately and unnecessarily hyped up the materials and the facts contained in the first information report in order to prosecute the accused-petitioner for harassment. We, therefore, find a good deal of force in the contention of Mr AKM Nazrul Islam that the very initiation of the criminal proceedings as well as the continuance of the same against the accused-petitioner would amount to an abuse of the process of the law as well as of the court and it is, therefore, necessary to quash the proceedings to secure the ends of justice. 

 15. We have given our anxious consideration to the facts and circumstances of the case. From the first information report it does not appear that the petitioner obtained or attempted to obtain any pecuniary advantage abusing his position as Chairman of the allotment committee. In the whole deal we do not find any element of mens rea on the part of the petitioner inasmuch as his actions appear to be bonafide. 

 The proceedings of Khulshi PS Case No. 40(6) 2002 dated 30-6-2000 corresponding to DAB,GR Case No. 12 of 2002, Khulshi PS Case No. 41(6)2002 dated 30-6-2002 corresponding to DAB, GR case No. 12 of 2002, Khulshi PS Case No. 42(6)2002 dated 30-6-2002 corresponding to DAB, GR Case No. 14 of 2002 and Khulshi PS Case No. 32(9) 2002 dated 25-9-2002 corresponding to DAB, GR Case No. 27 of 2002 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong so far as it relates to the accused petitioner, are quashed.
